what: Live production evidence that api/_mcp-studio forge_free defaults to the standard tier and that an explicit tier:'high' request really runs the high lane.
method: POST tools/call forge_free, then the forge_creations row for the returned creation id (authoritative tier/backend, not inferred from the response text).

runs.label: default (no tier argument)

arguments.prompt: a small ceramic teapot with a bamboo handle, glossy celadon glaze

runs.verdict: Default is the standard tier. Matches the tool schema, the submission answer sheet, and docs/mcp-studio.md.

runs.label: explicit tier:'high'

arguments.prompt: a friendly round robot mascot, glossy white plastic

runs.verdict: High is a real, working option served by the self-hosted async Hunyuan3D Cloud Run GPU worker (GCP_HUNYUAN3D_URL). It did not degrade to standard.

why_standard_stays_the_default: Neither lane finishes inside a ChatGPT tool-call window (164s standard, 144s high in this capture), so latency is not what separates them; forge_free hands back a pollable job handle when a generation outlives STUDIO_FORGE_TIMEOUT_MS.
The hunyuan3d worker is scale-to-zero, so a cold container adds a spin-up on top of the generation and the tail is materially worse than this warm sample.

The high-tier access gate is cleared only by the platform seed token (CRON_SECRET). A deployment without it would silently serve standard while any 'high by default' claim stayed on the page, which is the exact misstatement this evidence exists to prevent.
